User Story: As a returning coach, I want to resume or start a career so I can enter the coaching world.
Expected Behaviour: Load the primary save or backup; show recovery controls on load failure; offer new career setup and settings; do not silently create a new world when a save exists.
Edge Cases: No save; corrupt primary; valid backup; future schema; retry; cancel setup.
Validation Rules: Save envelope markers and schema are validated before decode; recovery actions remain explicit.
Known Assumptions: A valid local save is the only source of an existing career.
Test Cases: T-UI-001-H restore; T-UI-001-E corrupt/future save; T-UI-001-A VoiceOver and AX5.
Current Status: Implemented; unit and contract covered; live simulator unverified
Notes: Entry is routed from the shipped app root; no network or account dependency.

User Story: As a new player, I want to choose my coach identity, seed, and starting job so I can begin a deterministic career.
Expected Behaviour: Generate eligible starting jobs for the selected seed; accept bounded names and a programme ID; build and persist a new career; surface generation or stale-selection errors.
Edge Cases: Blank names; whitespace; names over 24 characters; stale programme ID; no eligible jobs; rapid seed changes; duplicate start taps.
Validation Rules: Trim names and cap each at 24 characters; require a UUID programme ID; ignore stale job requests; block duplicate starts.
Known Assumptions: Starting jobs are deterministic and generated off the main actor.
Test Cases: T-UI-002-H valid identity; T-UI-002-I stale programme; T-UI-002-B empty/long names; T-UI-002-C repeated taps.
Current Status: Implemented; provider and save paths covered; live form unverified
Notes: The form is a trust boundary for user input and must be manually checked at AX5.
Source Evidence: CoachWorldStore.swift; NewCareerCoachIdentityView.swift; Career session and save suite

User Story: As a coach seeking work, I want to inspect available jobs so I can choose my next appointment.
Expected Behaviour: Render career opportunities and route job-board actions to the composite Career Hub.

Validation Rules: Only opportunities present in the Career Hub model can be accepted.
Known Assumptions: Job Board is a legacy alias, not a separate persistent screen.
Test Cases: T-UI-003-H inspect and accept; T-UI-003-E stale/no opportunity; T-UI-003-N alias navigation.
Current Status: Implemented as alias to Career Hub; live journey unverified
Notes: Registry ID 3 resolves to screen 52.

User Story: As a coach with an opportunity, I want to review and accept or decline it with a clear consequence.
Expected Behaviour: Show the selected opportunity through Career Hub focus and allow accept or resignation actions.
Edge Cases: Opportunity disappears; accept twice; decline/resign; no current job.
Validation Rules: Stable opportunity IDs are parsed and revalidated by the store/session.
Known Assumptions: Offer is a legacy alias and uses the same model as Career Hub.
Test Cases: T-UI-004-H accept; T-UI-004-E stale ID; T-UI-004-C repeated action.
Current Status: Implemented as alias to Career Hub; live journey unverified
Notes: No separate Offer persistence model exists.

User Story: As an appointed coach, I want to see the appointment outcome so I know where my career now stands.
Expected Behaviour: Resolve Appointment through Career Hub focus and show the accepted current job or an actionable refusal.
Edge Cases: Appointment after resignation; missing career; stale saved route.
Validation Rules: Career control authority validates the appointment transition.
Known Assumptions: Appointment is a legacy entry alias.
Test Cases: T-UI-005-H accepted appointment; T-UI-005-E invalid transition; T-UI-005-R restore route.
Current Status: Implemented as alias to Career Hub; live journey unverified

User Story: As a player using assistive technology, I want settings and accessibility controls available before and during a career.
Expected Behaviour: Open settings from title and career navigation; close back to title or HQ; keep the dark palette and accessibility contracts.
Edge Cases: Open before save; open after restore; close from entry; AX5; VoiceOver; reduce motion.
Validation Rules: The surface is always included in available screens; controls have minimum targets and labels through shared contracts.

User Story: As a coach, I want to search the fictional football world so I can inspect programmes and teams.
Expected Behaviour: Provide a bounded search/read model of fictional identities and route team selection to a team profile.
Edge Cases: Empty query; no matches; duplicate names; selected team removed; long result lists.
Validation Rules: Results are derived from map and organisation IDs; selection must resolve to an existing organisation.
Known Assumptions: All identities are fictional and generated deterministically.
Test Cases: T-UI-007-H search/select; T-UI-007-E empty/no match; T-UI-007-L long results; T-UI-007-Legal fictional-name scan.
Current Status: Implemented; provider and legal suites covered; live journey unverified
Notes: No network search is expected.

User Story: As a head coach, I want a weekly command hub showing obligations, evidence, and the next action so I can run the season.
Expected Behaviour: Show the authoritative week, team, opponent, decisions, correspondence, preparation state, and actions to commit, delegate, inspect film, prepare, and advance.
Edge Cases: No opponent; pending decision; missing plans; delegated responsibility; save failure; no inbox item.
Validation Rules: Only intents in the read model are accepted; advance is refused until required plans exist; refusal copy is player-facing.
Known Assumptions: The read model never invents hidden facts; empty backing data is shown as unavailable.
Test Cases: T-UI-008-H inspect/prepare/advance; T-UI-008-E missing plans; T-UI-008-S stale intent; T-UI-008-A AX5/VoiceOver.
Current Status: Implemented; full suite and read-model tests passed; live week walkthrough unverified
Notes: G-05 from prior live critique is a regression risk; current refusal path is covered but the rendered status receipt needs device confirmation.

User Story: As a coach, I want to read correspondence and return to where I came from so I can act on information without losing context.
Expected Behaviour: List retained inbox items; mark items read; persist bounded read receipts; open supported routes; return to the origin route.
Edge Cases: Empty inbox; duplicate read; more than receipt cap; stale route; origin roster vs HQ.
Validation Rules: Stable IDs are required; read receipts are bounded; origin is encoded in presentation state.
Known Assumptions: Inbox is local presentation state backed by the save document.
Test Cases: T-UI-009-H open/mark read/return; T-UI-009-E stale item; T-UI-009-B receipt cap; T-UI-009-R save/restore.
Current Status: Implemented; persistence/read-model tests passed; live journey unverified
Notes: One HQ callback intentionally does not open correspondence and is a coverage gap to verify.

User Story: As a coach, I want observer-scoped opponent evidence so I can prepare without seeing hidden truth.
Expected Behaviour: Open retained tactical observations, show sample size/confidence/rates, and refuse when no current observation exists.
Edge Cases: No opponent; stale observation; zero samples; unavailable scout; open from match day vs HQ.
Validation Rules: Only observations keyed to the controlled observer/opponent/calendar are displayed; no current truth is substituted.
Known Assumptions: Scouting knowledge is distinct from hidden simulation truth.
Test Cases: T-UI-010-H inspect/open; T-UI-010-E missing/stale evidence; T-UI-010-P privacy of hidden values.
Current Status: Implemented; provider path covered; live observation display unverified
Notes: Film is intentionally limited to scouting, tactics, and replay.

User Story: As a coach, I want to set tactical identity before a week or match so the simulation uses my chosen plan.
Expected Behaviour: Display current tactical plan; allow valid plan changes; return to the origin; encode match tactical submissions with fixture and revision.
Edge Cases: Invalid/stale plan; open from match day; cancel; two concurrent updates; stale revision.
Validation Rules: Plan enum values must be valid; session revalidates fixture ID and revision.
Known Assumptions: Game plan is authoritative input, not a view-only preference.
Test Cases: T-UI-011-H set/return; T-UI-011-S stale match revision; T-UI-011-I invalid enum; T-UI-011-C concurrent action.
Current Status: Implemented; tactical suites passed; live journey unverified
Notes: The route is shared by weekly planning and in-match tactics.

User Story: As a coach, I want to choose practice emphasis so the week can advance with an intentional preparation plan.
Expected Behaviour: Show the practice plan and available choices; persist a valid selection; refuse week advancement until required preparation exists.
Edge Cases: No minutes; insufficient budget; stale option; repeated selection; accessibility text expansion.
Validation Rules: Minutes and plan values are validated by the tactical authority.
Known Assumptions: A plan must exist for advanceWeek when the authority requires it.
Test Cases: T-UI-012-H choose/advance; T-UI-012-B budget boundary; T-UI-012-S stale choice; T-UI-012-A AX5.
Current Status: Implemented; provider and tactical suites passed; live journey unverified
Notes: Weekly advance refusal is a high-value user journey.

User Story: As a coach, I want fatigue, injury, suspension, and condition evidence so I can manage availability.
Expected Behaviour: Show bounded player health statuses and aggregate condition/fatigue counts derived from lifecycle state.
Edge Cases: Empty roster; player missing lifecycle; 128+ statuses; injured and suspended player; zero average denominator.
Validation Rules: Rows are bounded to 128; empty averages use safe defaults; IDs must map to players.
Known Assumptions: Health is read-only on this surface and changes through simulation.
Test Cases: T-UI-013-H inspect health; T-UI-013-B empty/128 bound; T-UI-013-C injury/suspension evidence.
Current Status: Implemented; lifecycle suites passed; live journey unverified
Notes: Manual device review is needed for long generated names.

User Story: As a coach, I want to watch the current match and make bounded coaching calls without controlling players directly.
Expected Behaviour: Render the deterministic match checkpoint, score/field state, pause/takeover/advance controls, tactical plan and call-ins, and allow a truthful exit path.
Edge Cases: Match not started; match in progress; stale checkpoint; interruption; pause; final snap; no fixture.
Validation Rules: Intent IDs include fixture and revision; session refuses stale or invalid actions; no direct player control exists.
Known Assumptions: Canvas/Timeline render a 2D view; match decisions are coach-level only.
Test Cases: T-UI-014-H start/advance/call-in; T-UI-014-S stale revision; T-UI-014-B first/final snap; T-UI-014-A VoiceOver/control labels; T-UI-014-R rotate at install floor.
Current Status: Implemented; match and reducer suites passed; simulator/manual layout unverified
Notes: Prior UI review identified navigation/landscape risk; current code requires a real-device walk.

User Story: As a coach, I want a post-match receipt so I can understand what happened and continue the week.
Expected Behaviour: Show authoritative result and consequences; continue to HQ; open the detailed box score; persist route changes.
Edge Cases: No aftermath; close before persistence; draw/tie; missing box score; duplicate continue.
Validation Rules: Model must be present; box score route requires aftermath; result is read-only from engine output.
Known Assumptions: The aftermath is produced by the match authority.
Test Cases: T-UI-015-H continue/open box score; T-UI-015-E missing model; T-UI-015-C duplicate continue; T-UI-015-A AX5.
Current Status: Implemented; match/read-model paths covered; live journey unverified
Notes: Box score is a child route of the aftermath model.

User Story: As a coach, I want to inspect my roster so I can make personnel decisions.
Expected Behaviour: Show authoritative roster rows, positions, ratings/evidence, jersey numbers, status, and links to profiles/development/health.
Edge Cases: Empty roster; duplicate jersey numbers; injured player; long name; sort/filter; player unavailable.
Validation Rules: Rows derive from controlled programme/team ownership; jersey assignment is deterministic and bounded.

User Story: As a coach, I want to assign depth and personnel packages so the game uses the roster roles I intend.
Expected Behaviour: Display position units and valid placements; allow supported depth/personnel-plan selections; reject invalid or stale actions.
Edge Cases: Missing position coverage; duplicate player; empty unit; invalid package; long names.
Validation Rules: Position eligibility and minimum playable coverage are enforced by model/rules.

User Story: As a coach, I want a player profile with development evidence so I can make informed personnel decisions.
Expected Behaviour: Open a selected controlled-roster player; show authoritative identity, ratings, health, history, and development evidence; return to roster.

User Story: As a coach, I want to inspect development evidence so I can understand why a player changed.

User Story: As a coach, I want to inspect employed staff and their roles so I can understand delegated responsibilities.

User Story: As a coach, I want to understand scheme identity and fit so I can choose tactics deliberately.

User Story: As a coach, I want to choose personnel packages so my tactical plan matches available players.
Expected Behaviour: Resolve through the Depth Chart host and allow only valid personnel plans.

User Story: As a college coach, I want a bounded board of prospects so I can invest limited recruiting resources.
Expected Behaviour: List board and discovery prospects with observer-specific evaluations, costs, availability, and actions to contact/evaluate/visit/offer/withdraw.

Expected Behaviour: Open a selected board/discovery prospect; show evidence, fit, status, and available actions; return to board.

Notes: Commitment coverage validates every backticked PRODUCT gate, including both soak commands and LegalTests, against SuiteCatalog and main.swift. SuiteCatalog.Disposition now distinguishes .runnable from .unwritten(reason:spec:); AgencyBudgetTests cites OPEN-DECISIONS.md D1 (presentation-time constants are proposals, not measurements), PerformanceBudgetTests cites D4 (already known-red on host at 2.83s vs a 2.0s ceiling, road-to-beta.md B-4), TwoTierConsistencyTests cites D3 (depends on P5's unbuilt abstracted model), and SmallestDeviceLayoutTest cites D15/G-09 (needs a view host this headless harness does not have). A named test asserts the unwritten set stays exactly these four, so a fifth cannot go silently unwritten and closing one requires deliberately editing the list. Unwritten is not unverified-and-ignored: each entry still needs the cited spec resolved before it can graduate. The named legal gate passes 22 tests/141 checks. The 20-season soak command is mapped but did not complete after 35 minutes at roughly 1 GB RSS, so save-size/lifecycle evidence remains open. The timing command remains a probe, not a PerformanceBudget gate. SuiteCatalog.lane(for:) values (performance, persistence, legal) still do not match scripts/verify.sh's --lane vocabulary; flagged for the owner rather than forced, since the two serve different purposes (domain grouping vs. curated command dispatch) and reconciling them is a design decision, not a small fix.
